plainLanguage: Section 61 limits when compulsion can be relied on as a defence for an oath or engagement under section 60 and imposes a fourteen-day disclosure requirement, subject to the stated force or sickness qualification.
meaning: Ufafanuzi wa section 61 lazima ufuate complete statutory text, qualifications na procedural requirements zake; label ya offence pekee haitoshi.
keyPoints: The provision concerns oaths/engagements referred to in section 60.
Compulsion is not enough by itself; statutory disclosure conditions apply.
Ordinary period is fourteen days after taking the oath.
Actual force or sickness can shift the start of the fourteen-day period.
Disclosure must include the whole of what the person knows concerning the matter.

legalTerms.meaning: Maana na scope yake huamuliwa na exact wording ya statutory provision na authoritative interpretation.

history.summary: Section 61 is recorded in The Penal Code [CAP. 16 R.E. 2022].
notes: Official text was audited before this explanation was added.

expertPerspectives.label: Mtazamo A
expertPerspectives.view: Each statutory element and qualification should be analysed separately.

expertPerspectives.label: Mtazamo B
expertPerspectives.view: Where the section states a procedural safeguard or consent requirement, it should be treated as part of the legal analysis.
